applies_why: This judge text calls the Isaiah 7:14 link UNDERDETERMINED partly by treating the almah/bethulah word-count that cuts both ways as leaving the matter open.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: ‘A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand’ — weighed: (1) two-sense material cannot ground UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand; (2) two senses can leave the link open.
why: The judge treats the two-way almah/bethulah word-count as an openness reason for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2’s command that a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand.
